2026"],"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.18653\/v1\/2026.findings-acl.209","type":"proceedings-article"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Language models are routinely given long, multispan inputs assembled from documents, chat history, tool outputs, and memory entries. When the model generates a response, it may draw on spans that are irrelevant to the query and produce a confident, coherent answer grounded in the wrong part of the context. This paper argues that such failures constitute a distinct phenomenon, which we call Ghost Context, and that the existing taxonomy of hallucination does not adequately capture them. A hallucinating model invents information that is absent from context. A model exhibiting Ghost Context uses information that is present but should not influence the current output. The error is not fabrication; it is misattribution. Critically, Ghost Context can occur even when every span in the context is individually authorized for the user and permissible for the application, making it difficult to detect for access control mechanisms and standard faithfulness checks that treat the context as an undifferentiated pool of evidence. We formalize Ghost Context, propose a taxonomy of four interference patterns, describe a mask-and-rerun detection methodology, and outline the security implications for retrieval-augmented generation and agent memory systems. We argue that reliable deployment of long-context models requires distinguishing Ghost Context from conventional hallucination and developing targeted mitigation strategies for cross-context interference.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Ghost Context: Cross-Context Hallucination in Long-Context Language Models"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0003-8516-0723","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Rohith","family":"Namboothiri","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,20]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1"},{"DOI":"10.18653\/v1\/2025.naacl-long.624","title":["DeCAP: Context-Adaptive Prompt Generation for Debiasing Zero-shot Question Answering in Large Language Models"],"author":[{"given":"Suyoung","family":"Bae","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"YunSeok","family":"Choi","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Jee-Hyong","family":"Lee","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025]]},"container-title":["Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)"],"is-referenced-by-count":2,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.18653\/v1\/2025.naacl-long.624","type":"proceedings-article"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>The rapid increase in unstructured data across various fields has made multi-document comprehension and summarization a critical task. This paper explores the use of Long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) for multi-document summarization, demonstrating their exceptional capacity to grasp extensive connections, provide cohesive summaries, and adapt to various industry domains and integration with enterprise applications\/systems. The paper discusses the workflow of multi-document summarization for effectively deploying long-context LLMs, supported by case studies in legal applications, enterprise functions such as HR, finance, and sourcing, as well as in the medical and news domains. These case studies show notable enhancements in both efficiency and accuracy. Technical obstacles, such as dataset diversity, model scalability, and ethical considerations like bias mitigation and factual accuracy, are carefully analyzed.
